items.title: AI领域Q1融资额超2025全年——《24小时太阳报》
items.snippet: 2026年第一季度全球AI产业融资总额已超越2025年全年水平，资本持续涌入人工智能赛道。
items.raw_snippet: In the first quarter of 2026, the global artificial intelligence market for private (unlisted) companies experienced unprecedented growth, with the total amount raised amounting to **$226 billion in 1,965 deals** globally. A single transaction was the key driver of the market: the $122 billion round closed in early April by OpenAI for a post-money valuation of**$852 billion**, which alone accounted for 54% of the quarter's total funding. The period was dominated by mega-rounds: deals in excess of USD 100m catalysed 94% of capital raised, up from 80% in the previous quarter. Target companies acquired by the leading incumbents have **an average time to exit of 4.5 years**, significantly shorter than the 7.6-year average recorded for AI M&A deals in the quarter as a whole. Overall, the picture that emerges from the quarter thus shows three main trends: quarterly revenues already exceeding the 2025 annual total, driven by model developers; the entry into a consolidation phase for 'physical AI'; and intense M&A activity by big tech, reflecting the growing strategic urgency to strengthen positioning in artificial intelligence.

items.raw_snippet: # SpaceX Strikes Deal With Cursor for $60 Billion. SpaceX said a deal with Cursor gave it the option to buy the artificial intelligence start-up, which makes code-writing software, for $60 billion later this year. SpaceX, Elon Musk’s rocket and satellite company, said on Tuesday that it had struck a deal with the artificial intelligence start-up Cursor that could result in its acquiring the young company for $60 billion. SpaceX added that the agreement gave it the option “to acquire Cursor later this year for $60 billion or pay $10 billion for our work together.” It is unclear if the companies plan to consummate the deal before or after SpaceX’s I.P.O., which could happen as early as June. In February, SpaceX acquired xAI, Mr. Musk’s A.I. start-up, in a transaction that valued the combined company at $1.25 trillion, according to information sent to investors. items.raw_snippet: # SpaceX Secures $60 Billion Option to Acquire AI Coding Giant Cursor. Elon Musk’s space and technology company SpaceX has secured the right to acquire AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion still this year. For the development of its products, Cursor uses AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Google, but also has its own in-house LLM called “Composer,” which is also based on a Chinese open-source model. SpaceX stated that both companies are working together to “create the world’s best AI for coding and knowledge work.” Cursor is set to build on SpaceX’s massive computing capacities, including the Colossus supercomputer in Memphis, which was built within 122 days. With the acquisition of Cursor, SpaceX would acquire an existing customer base among software developers as well as proven products, rather than building this position organically. One detail attracting attention ahead of the possible acquisition: the latest version of Cursor’s own Composer model was developed on the basis of an open-source model from Chinese startup Moonshot AI.

items.snippet: 苹果任命硬件工程负责人John Ternus为新任CEO，蒂姆·库克将转任执行董事长，继续参与公司战略决策。
items.raw_snippet: Apple has named longtime hardware executive John Ternus as its next chief executive officer, marking a major leadership transition as the company seeks to strengthen its position in the artificial intelligence era. Ternus will take over as CEO on 1 September, while Tim Cook will remain with the company as executive chairman, Apple said on Monday. Cook, who has led Apple for 15 years and oversaw a dramatic expansion in its market value, is handing over leadership as the company faces mounting pressure to innovate in AI, an area where critics say it has lagged. Analysts say Ternus is likely to focus on building a stronger in-house AI strategy while also pushing forward with new hardware categories, including foldable devices, augmented reality products, and next-generation personal computing. Like Cook before him, Ternus assumes the top role after decades inside the company, suggesting Apple is prioritizing stability as it navigates technological and geopolitical challenges, including supply chain pressures and the race to define the next generation of AI-powered devices.
